standard.python: n/a - no Python in the repository

tasks.title: Source does not build under the audit standard (Swift 6 language mode, strict concurrency, warnings-as-errors)
tasks.evidence_before: AUDIT/baseline/strict-concurrency.txt: rc=1, 22 errors + 20 warnings. Kinds: 3x non-Sendable static ISO8601DateFormatter/publicURL, 4x main-actor-isolated top-level lets (TRANSIENT, tlsIdentity, peerURL) referenced from nonisolated code, 2x DispatchWorkItem capture, 18x captured-var mutation / non-Sendable capture in @Sendable closures.
tasks.fix_summary: Umbrella task. Sub-tasks 0002-0005 carry the actual diffs; this closes when `xcrun swiftc -swift-version 6 -strict-concurrency=complete -warnings-as-errors` is clean for chatbox.swift and chatbox-mcp.swift and the documented build/README state the same flags.
tasks.notes: Existing `@unchecked Sendable` on Chatbox/Store is the reason the checker is silent today; the brief forbids adding it as a fix. The serial-queue invariant is real, so the fix is to express it (see 0005), not to annotate it away.

tasks.title: Static ISO8601DateFormatter instances are shared mutable state (not Sendable)
tasks.evidence_before: chatbox.swift:1062:16: error: static property 'iso' is not concurrency-safe because non-'Sendable' type 'ISO8601DateFormatter' may have shared mutable state; same at 1070 for 'isoTiny'.
tasks.fix_summary: Replace the two formatters with `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle` (Sendable) or per-call formatting; keep the fractional-seconds fallback parse. Must not regress the hot path (`nowISO()` is called per write).
tasks.notes: Rejected: `nonisolated(unsafe)` - same escape hatch as @unchecked Sendable, forbidden as a fix.

tasks.title: `Chatbox.publicURL` is a mutable static global
tasks.evidence_before: chatbox.swift:1238:16: error: static property 'publicURL' is not concurrency-safe because it is nonisolated global shared mutable state.
tasks.fix_summary: Make the public URL an immutable value produced once from configuration and passed into Chatbox (used by usage()/`GET /`), removing the static var.

tasks.title: Top-level configuration `let`s are MainActor-isolated and referenced from nonisolated code
tasks.evidence_before: chatbox.swift:3215:22 error: main actor-isolated var 'peerURL' can not be referenced from a nonisolated context (x2); 3217/3221 'tlsIdentity'; 27:1 'TRANSIENT'.
tasks.fix_summary: Move startup configuration into a `Sendable` struct (or make the file a library with an explicit entry point) so the listener/shutdown code receives immutable config instead of reaching for globals. TRANSIENT (sqlite destructor sentinel) becomes a nonisolated immutable constant.
tasks.notes: Root cause is that top-level code in a single-file executable is implicitly @MainActor under Swift 6 mode.

tasks.title: Non-Sendable captures and captured-var mutation across @Sendable closures (DispatchWorkItem, URLSession completion, waiters, event poll)
tasks.evidence_before: 20 warnings promoted to errors: capture of 'idle' DispatchWorkItem; 6x mutation of captured var (answer, status, redirectedTo, req, touch, nextKeep); 2x capture of 'waiter'.
tasks.fix_summary: Replace the completion-handler + semaphore shapes with async/await (`URLSession.data(for:)`) or `Synchronization.Mutex`-protected boxes, and stop capturing mutable vars: values cross actor/queue boundaries as immutable results. Keep the documented single-serial-queue invariant expressed in types.
tasks.notes: This is the core of 0001 and the largest single change in the audit.

tasks.title: CI actions are pinned to mutable tags, not commit SHAs
tasks.fix_summary: Pin each action to a full commit SHA with the tag in a comment; record the update procedure.

tasks.title: 63 force-unwrapped String.data(using:.utf8)! conversions
tasks.fix_summary: Use the non-failable `Data(_:)` initializer (or a tiny helper) so no `!` remains on a conversion that cannot fail.

tasks.title: Variable interpolated into a printf format string (SC2059)
tasks.evidence_before: SC2059 (info) 'Don't use variables in the printf format string' - a value containing % is reinterpreted as a directive.
tasks.fix_summary: Pass the value as an argument to printf '%s' with a fixed format.

tasks.title: A pipeline both reads and writes the same file (SC2094) - truncation/data-loss risk
tasks.evidence_before: SC2094 x2 'Make sure not to read and write the same file in the same pipeline'.
tasks.fix_summary: Read into a variable or write to a temporary file and move it into place atomically; never redirect into a file the same pipeline is reading.

tasks.title: Shellcheck findings in the suite (SC3057 x3 quoted substring, SC2143 x5, SC2059 x2, SC2034, SC2329)
tasks.evidence_before: AUDIT/baseline/shellcheck-suite.txt - 12 findings; SC3057 is a real parsing hazard in parameter expansion.
tasks.fix_summary: Triage each: fix the real ones (SC3057/SC2059) and add targeted directives with justification where the pattern is deliberate.
tasks.notes: A check that silently mis-parses is a vacuous check (the file's own design rule).

tasks.title: Formatter/linter baseline: 3309 swift-format findings, 303 swiftlint findings
tasks.evidence_before: AUDIT/baseline/swift-format.txt (3309), AUDIT/baseline/swiftlint-counts.txt (303: identifier_name 124, line_length 83, non_optional_string_data_conversion 63, cyclomatic_complexity 8, ...)
tasks.fix_summary: Add a committed formatter config matching the project's real style, apply it in one formatting-only commit, and keep swiftlint's substantive rules on while disabling the ones that fight documented design (file_length for the single-file constraint) with a written reason.
tasks.notes: Formatting must be its own commit, never mixed into a fix (brief S10).

tasks.title: Documented toolchain (Swift 6.3.3) contradicts the audit standard (Swift 6.4 + strict concurrency)
tasks.evidence_before: chatbox.swift header: 'Swift 6.3.3, Foundation + Network + SQLite3 only'; README build line has no language mode or strictness flags.
tasks.fix_summary: Update the documented build to the flags that are actually required, in the same commit as the code that satisfies them (0001).

tasks.title: Unbounded scratch growth: 1.8 GB / 120414 files from mutation runs and per-cell TLS fixtures
tasks.evidence_before: du -sh tests/.scratch = 1.8G; find | wc -l = 120414; gitleaks worktree scan took 71s over 1.34 GB and reported 2097 hits, 100% under tests/.scratch (1048 pkcs12-file + 1048 private-key from the TLS fixture, 1 false positive in mut/names.json).
tasks.fix_summary: Have the harness prune per-cell scratch (keep only the failing cell's artefacts) and delete the accumulated directory once no run is active. Command + rollback are logged in the ledger before running.
tasks.notes: Tracked tree and full history are clean (gitleaks: 0 leaks in 42 commits, 0 in git archive HEAD).

tasks.title: CodeQL swift/cleartext-transmission (high) on the HTTP listener - waiver or design change
tasks.evidence_before: 1 open code-scanning alert #1 swift/cleartext-transmission, severity high, chatbox.swift:2426. TLS is opt-in by documented design (README/Deployment/Architecture), so the alert is accurate rather than a false positive.
tasks.fix_summary: Decision task: (a) keep plaintext support and record a written waiver in the repo (AUDIT/waivers.md) plus a CodeQL dismissal with the same justification, or (b) make TLS mandatory (breaking every client URL and the documented deployment). Recommendation: (a) - the channel is documented for private networks and the client already supports TLS; forcing it is a product decision, not a defect fix.
tasks.notes: Rejected as a fix: silencing CodeQL. The alert stays visible unless a human decision says otherwise.

tasks.title: `@unchecked Sendable` on Chatbox and Store suppresses all concurrency checking
tasks.evidence_before: final class Chatbox: @unchecked Sendable; final class Store: @unchecked Sendable. Every cross-thread access in the file relies on this promise; the compiler therefore reports nothing today (the 0001 baseline shows what it would report without it).
tasks.fix_summary: Either express the serial-queue invariant in types the compiler can check (a global actor or an actor per store) or keep the annotation with an explicit, reviewed invariant comment *and* keep all current and future calls on the queue - decision recorded; the brief forbids adding such annotations, so the audit's default is the typed model.
tasks.notes: Overlaps 0001/0005; kept separate because it is the reviewable decision, not the mechanical fix.

tasks.title: SC1090: the client sources a non-constant path (~/.chatbox)
tasks.evidence_before: SC1090 (warning): ShellCheck can't follow non-constant source.
tasks.fix_summary: Add a `# shellcheck source=/dev/null` directive with a comment explaining that the path is the documented config file, and confirm the file is only read (never executed from an untrusted location).
tasks.notes: Sourcing a shell file executes it: check the ownership/permission expectations of ~/.chatbox.
